notes: Real HTTP 404 with a large branded error page (267KB decompressed). Page size is not a 404 signal.

distinguishing_from: Textbook 404: correct status AND explicit copy, in German. Note that no English not-found string appears anywhere, so English-only keyword lists fail on this file.
notes: Smallest real 404 collected (18KB, 268 visible-text chars). Also notable: this host serves a consent wall on its homepage but NOT on its 404 page.

distinguishing_from: Correct 404 status but served with the site's FULL navigation (268KB decompressed), larger than several successful pages in this corpus. Confirms body size is orthogonal to error state.
notes: Contrast with paywall_saas/statista_statistic.html from the same host: same chrome, different status and different gating markup.

distinguishing_from: A 404 page that ALSO carries the site's age-gate markup. One document, two categories. Any single-label classifier is wrong on this file no matter which label it picks.
notes: 144KB. Strong argument for multi-label output over single-label classification.

distinguishing_from: WRONG-STATUS CASE: a missing page answered with HTTP 400 Bad Request, not 404, and the copy says something-went-wrong rather than not-found. Neither the status nor the text says missing.
notes: Closest thing to a soft-404 collected. Shows that status-to-category mapping needs a 4xx bucket, not a 404 equality test.

distinguishing_from: NEGATIVE CONTROL and the hardest file here: HTTP 200 after a 307/302/302/302 chain across two domains, 20KB of HTML, and SIX visible-text characters. It is not a 404, not a login page, and not a wall; it is an empty client-rendered shell.
notes: Any almost-no-text-means-blocked rule fires here and is wrong. Without executing JavaScript the true state is genuinely unknowable.
